sources.entry: Web Browser Engineering: this book explains how to build a basic but complete web browser, from networking to JavaScript, in a couple thousand lines of Python.

summary.title: Web Browser Engineering
summary.one_liner: You learn how a web browser works by building a basic but complete one, from networking and HTML parsing through layout, CSS, JavaScript, and compositing, in a couple thousand lines of Python.
keywords: write a web browser in python
takeaways: Download web pages by working with URLs and HTTP requests
Draw to a window and lay out formatted, word-wrapped text
Parse and fix HTML into a tree, then apply inline and block layout
Parse and apply CSS, and handle links, buttons, and form submission
Run scripts that change the DOM and react to events, plus cookies, XSS and CSRF basics
Cover the event loop, compositing, GPU animations, accessibility, and invalidation
summary.summary: Web Browser Engineering is a book that explains how web browsers work by building a basic but complete browser, from networking to JavaScript, in a couple thousand lines of Python. The table of contents is organized into chapters that each add one browser subsystem: downloading pages, drawing and text formatting, HTML tree construction, layout, CSS styling, links and chrome, form submission, scripting, cookies and security, visual effects, threading and the event loop, animation, accessibility, embedded content, and incremental recomputation. The listing describes it as available in print and in Korean and Japanese translations, with a book blog and a GitHub discussion forum. The page text is mostly a table of contents and promotional links, so details beyond the chapter list are not given.
